topic: Rust for backend engineers: building crumbs
goal: Backend engineer (Python/JS) learning Rust; publish all work publicly on GitHub; extend to Deep-level modules later

modules.title: Why is the compiler yelling at me?
modules.summary: Install the toolchain, ship a first binary, and model a log line with Rust's type system.
objectives: Create, build and run a Cargo project in debug and release mode
Use bindings, mutability, shadowing and the core scalar types deliberately
Model domain data with structs and enums and branch on it exhaustively with match

lessons.title: Hello cargo: ship a binary
lessons.summary: Install rustup, create crumbs with cargo, run it, and see why release builds matter.
objectives: Install the Rust toolchain on Windows and verify rustc/cargo
Explain what cargo new, cargo run, cargo build and cargo build --release produce
Read a compiler error and fix it from the message alone
Read command-line arguments with std::env::args and print them

lessons.title: Variables, types, mutability, shadowing
lessons.summary: Why let is immutable by default, what the integer types are for, and when shadowing beats mut.
objectives: Choose between let, let mut and shadowing and justify the choice
Pick appropriate integer and float types and predict overflow behaviour in debug vs release
Write functions with typed parameters and return values, using expressions vs statements correctly
Count lines in a file passed on the command line

lessons.title: Structs, enums and match: modelling a log line
lessons.summary: Turn a raw nginx access-log line into a typed LogEntry with an HttpMethod enum.
objectives: Define structs with impl blocks and associated functions
Define enums with data and match on them exhaustively
Use Option to represent a field that may be missing
Explain why exhaustive match prevents a whole class of bugs

test.title: Module 1 check
test.summary: Cargo, types, functions, structs, enums and match.

modules.title: Who owns this string?
modules.summary: Ownership, moves and borrowing: the rules that replace a garbage collector.
objectives: Predict when a value is moved, copied or cloned
Borrow immutably and mutably within the aliasing-XOR-mutation rule
Parse text with slices instead of allocating new Strings
Diagnose and fix common borrow-checker errors from their error codes

lessons.title: Moves, clone and Copy
lessons.summary: Why let b = a broke your code, and what Python was doing behind your back.
objectives: Explain ownership and drop in terms of who frees the memory
Predict which types are Copy and which move
Decide when clone is the right fix and when it hides a design problem

lessons.title: Borrowing: shared and mutable references
lessons.summary: & and &mut, and the one rule the borrow checker enforces.
objectives: Pass values by reference into functions instead of moving them
State the aliasing-XOR-mutation rule and apply it to a code sample
Explain non-lexical lifetimes: why a borrow ends at its last use

lessons.title: Slices: &str vs String and zero-copy parsing
lessons.summary: Split log lines into fields without allocating a single new String.
objectives: Explain the memory layout difference between String and &str
Write functions that accept &str and work with both literals and Strings
Parse a log line into borrowed slices and explain why the line must outlive them

lessons.title: Bug hunt: reading borrow-checker errors
lessons.summary: Five broken crumbs functions, five error codes, zero unnecessary clones.
objectives: Read E0382, E0499, E0502 and E0505 and identify the conflicting borrows
Fix each by restructuring rather than cloning
Explain why each original program would have been unsafe in C

test.title: Module 2 check
test.summary: Ownership, borrowing, slices, plus Module 1 fundamentals.

modules.title: What happens when the input is garbage?
modules.summary: Errors as values, collections, iterators, and streaming huge files.
objectives: Handle absence and failure with Option and Result instead of panics
Propagate errors with ? through custom error types
Aggregate data with Vec, HashMap and iterator chains
Stream a multi-gigabyte file in bounded memory and benchmark it

lessons.title: Option and Result: no null, no exceptions
lessons.summary: Malformed log lines stop being crashes and become values you handle.
objectives: Convert panicking code (unwrap, indexing) into Option/Result-returning code
Use match, if let, map, and_then and unwrap_or appropriately
Explain when unwrap or expect is acceptable

lessons.title: The ? operator and custom errors
lessons.summary: One ParseError enum, thiserror for the library, anyhow for main.
objectives: Propagate errors with ? and explain the From conversion it performs
Define a custom error enum with thiserror
Choose between thiserror and anyhow and justify it

lessons.title: Vec, HashMap, iterators and closures
lessons.summary: Top-10 slowest endpoints in a single iterator chain.
objectives: Build and query Vec and HashMap, including the entry API
Write iterator chains with map, filter, fold and collect
Explain closure capture modes (borrow, mutable borrow, move)
Explain why iterator chains compile to loops (zero-cost abstraction)

lessons.title: Streaming 4 GB with BufReader: Rust vs Python
lessons.summary: Process a huge log in constant memory and benchmark against the 11-minute Python script.
objectives: Read a file line by line with BufReader without loading it into memory
Avoid per-line allocations by reusing a buffer
Benchmark debug vs release vs Python fairly and report results honestly

test.title: Module 3 check
test.summary: Error handling, collections, iterators, I/O, plus ownership.

modules.title: How do I structure a real Rust project?
modules.summary: Traits, generics, modules, a proper CLI, and tests.
objectives: Define and implement traits, including derived standard traits
Write generic functions and types with trait bounds
Split a crate into modules and a lib + bin and add a clap CLI
Write unit, integration and doc tests

lessons.title: Traits and derive
lessons.summary: Teach LogEntry to print itself, compare itself and render as table or JSON.
objectives: Derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash and explain what each enables
Implement Display and a custom OutputFormat trait
Compare Rust traits to Python protocols/ABCs and TS interfaces

lessons.title: Generics and trait bounds
lessons.summary: One stats function that works over any source of log lines.
objectives: Write generic functions with bounds and where clauses
Accept impl Iterator / impl Trait arguments and return types
Explain monomorphisation vs dyn Trait and pick one for a given case

lessons.title: Modules, lib + bin, and clap
lessons.summary: Turn crumbs from one main.rs into a real crate with a real CLI.
objectives: Organise code into modules with pub/private visibility
Split a package into lib.rs and main.rs and explain why
Add dependencies in Cargo.toml and build a subcommand CLI with clap derive

lessons.title: Testing: unit, integration and doc tests
lessons.summary: Lock down the parser before you make it fast.
objectives: Write unit tests with #[cfg(test)] and assert macros
Write integration tests in tests/ against the public API
Write doc tests that double as documentation

test.title: Module 4 check
test.summary: Traits, generics, project structure, testing, plus error handling.

modules.title: Can it use all my cores?
modules.summary: Lifetimes, smart pointers, threads and the async mental model.
objectives: Annotate lifetimes where the compiler needs them and explain what they mean
Choose between Box, Rc, Arc and interior mutability
Parallelise work safely with threads and rayon
Explain how async/await and tokio schedule work

lessons.title: Lifetimes: what 'a actually means
lessons.summary: A struct that borrows its log line, and the annotation that makes it compile.
objectives: Explain lifetime annotations as relationships, not durations you set
Apply the elision rules to predict when annotations are needed
Write a struct holding &'a str fields and use it correctly

lessons.title: Box, Rc, Arc and interior mutability
lessons.summary: When single ownership isn't enough.
objectives: Use Box for heap allocation and trait objects
Use Rc/Arc for shared ownership and explain the cost
Use RefCell/Mutex for interior mutability and explain when it panics or blocks

lessons.title: Threads, Send/Sync and rayon
lessons.summary: Parse the 4 GB log on every core with no data races.
objectives: Spawn threads and share state with Arc<Mutex<T>> or channels
Explain Send and Sync and read the errors when they are violated
Parallelise an iterator with rayon and measure the speedup

lessons.title: async/await and tokio
lessons.summary: The mental model you need before writing a server.
objectives: Explain futures as lazy state machines driven by an executor
Write async functions and run them concurrently on tokio
Explain why blocking inside async is a bug and how to avoid it

test.title: Module 5 check
test.summary: Lifetimes, smart pointers, concurrency, async, plus earlier modules.

modules.title: Ship it as a service
modules.summary: crumbs becomes crumbs-server: an HTTP API with a database, tracing and CI.
objectives: Serialise and deserialise JSON with serde
Build an axum HTTP API with routing, extractors and shared state
Persist and query data with sqlx and SQLite
Map errors to HTTP responses, add tracing, and run tests in GitHub Actions

lessons.title: serde: JSON in and out
lessons.summary: Derive Serialize/Deserialize and control the wire format.
objectives: Derive Serialize and Deserialize and customise with attributes
Handle optional and unknown fields deliberately
Explain how serde's derive avoids runtime reflection

lessons.title: An HTTP API with axum
lessons.summary: Routes, extractors and shared state for ingesting and querying logs.
objectives: Define routes and handlers with Path, Query, Json and State extractors
Share application state safely across handlers
Compare axum's model to FastAPI/Express

lessons.title: Persistence with sqlx and SQLite
lessons.summary: Store ingested entries and query stats with compile-time-checked SQL.
objectives: Set up a connection pool and run migrations
Write queries with sqlx and map rows to structs
Explain what compile-time query checking buys you and costs you

lessons.title: Errors as responses, tracing and CI
lessons.summary: Production polish: IntoResponse errors, structured logs and a green pipeline.
objectives: Implement IntoResponse for an application error type
Add structured logging with tracing
Run fmt, clippy and tests in GitHub Actions

test.title: Module 6 check
test.summary: serde, axum, sqlx, error handling, CI, plus the whole course.

finalProject.title: crumbs-server
finalProject.summary: A log ingestion and query service that replaces the 11-minute Python script: ingest nginx logs over HTTP, persist them, and answer 'what broke at 3am?' in milliseconds.
requirements: Ingest endpoint accepting raw nginx log lines; malformed lines reported, never crash the server
Query endpoints for stats by endpoint, status code and time window, backed by SQLite via sqlx
Library/binary split with unit and integration tests covering parser and API
Application error type mapped to proper HTTP responses; structured tracing logs
GitHub Actions CI running fmt, clippy and tests, green on main
Dockerfile producing a small release image
README with architecture overview and an honest Rust-vs-Python benchmark
stretch: Per-client rate limiting with tower middleware
Streaming endpoint (SSE) that tails new errors live
